title: Donkey figurines against li'bu-fever
eyebrow: CTH 811 · Babylonian healing ritual copied at Ḫattuša

dating.label: Ḫattuša copy, 14th–13th c. BCE (approx.)
dating.note: Found in the Great Temple storerooms at Boğazköy; the copy is not in Boğazköy ductus (Bácskay 2018). This dates the manuscript context, not the Babylonian composition.

purpose: Remove the 'seizure' of li'bu-fever of the mountain by sending a clay substitute of the patient, riding a provisioned clay donkey, out to the open country before Šamaš.
editionLabel: Hethitologie-Portal Mainz concordance, CTH 811; A. Bácskay, AOAT 447 (2018) 164–176

phases.name: Make the figures
phases.idea: Donkey figurines and a clothed substitute are made from clay mixed with urine, hair and nail-parings.

phases.name: On the roof before Šamaš
phases.idea: The figures are brought before Šamaš on the roof with a strewn offering and address.

phases.name: Dispatch the substitute
phases.idea: The substitute is taken to the open country and the evil handed to it and adjured away.

phases.name: Ešegu-bush and city gate
phases.idea: The ešegu-bush is seized as intercessor; designs, loaves and flour close the way back through the city gate.

phases.name: Further remedy
phases.idea: One legible alternative remedy for recurrent fever.
